subject: ela
intro: Seventh graders analyze how an author develops and contrasts the points of view of different characters or narrators in a text. Different characters may see the same event differently, and the author uses this contrast to build irony, sympathy, or understanding. Dramatic irony occurs when the reader knows something a character does not.

items.prompt:
Read.

The reader knows the 'treasure map' is a prank, but Theo excitedly follows it, sure he'll be rich.

What is this contrast between the reader's and Theo's knowledge called?

steps: When the reader knows more than the character, it is dramatic irony.

items.prompt:
Read.

To Mom, the move meant a fresh start; to her daughter, it meant leaving every friend behind.

How does the author use contrasting points of view?

steps: The two characters see the same event oppositely.
The author shows the move is hopeful for one and painful for the other.
So the contrast reveals how the same event affects characters differently.
solution.answer: It shows the same event means hope to one and loss to the other.

items.prompt: Why might an author give characters CONTRASTING points of view?

steps: Contrasting views create tension, irony, or deeper understanding.
So it builds tension and helps readers understand multiple sides.
solution.answer: To build tension/irony and show multiple sides.

items.prompt: When the reader knows more than a character, it is ____ irony.
Two characters seeing one event differently shows ____ points of view.
A first-person narrator shares only ____ character's view.
